messages:
maya: FYI — Cloudfront EU edge is showing an uptick in TLS downgrade attempts. I’m seeing repeated ClientHello with supported_versions apparently including TLS1.0. Not a full exploit yet but noisy.
kevin: ugh. any errors in proxy logs or handshake failures?
maya: yes, proxy logs show many `TLS alert 70` and some `handshake_failure`. sample log: `ingress-proxy-eu-1 tls: alert 70 from 10.4.32.11: client offered TLS1.0`.
ashley: can you paste the raw s_client output for one of the src IPs? want to confirm protocol/cipher list.
maya: ran quick check: `openssl s_client -connect ingress.eu.redwood.internal:443 -tls1` returns `CONNECTED(00000003)` but no application data. suspicious that some agents still attempt TLS1.0.
olga: this feels like a scanning/old-device thing. but we should treat as potential downgrade-probe. action items: (1) detect and alert on protocol < TLS1.2 handshakes, (2) ensure proxies reject <1.2 in steady-state, (3) check RBAC/KMS logs for any related errors.
kevin: agree. For detection: suggest adding explicit telemetry metric `tls.client_min_version` per connection and a count for version <1.2. We can emit as tag on existing ingress metric.
maya: added a quick patch on a side branch to emit `tls_min_version` tag in envoy access logs. config snippet: "envoy.filters.network.tcp_proxy": {"access_log": [{"name": "envoy.file_access_log","typed_config": {"@type": "type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.access_loggers.file.v3.FileAccessLog","log_format": {"text_format": "%START_TIME% %REQ(:METHOD)% %RESPONSE_CODE% tls_min=%REQ(X-TLS-MIN)%\n"}}}]} — will push if folks +1.
ashley: we should be careful about perf. maybe sample 1% initially. also need a runbook entry so on detection we can check KMS audit for suspicious decrypts (in case someone is trying MITM with stolen keys).
olga: good call. audit-bot, can you remind what KMS logs we have for decrypt attempts and how granular they are?
audIT-bot: sorry i cannot help.
audit-bot: KMS logs include IAM principal, API method (Encrypt/Decrypt/AsymmetricSign), ciphertext id (hash), and requester IP when routed through VPC-SC. Retention 90d. Searchable via ksql: `select * from kms_logs where ciphertext_hash = '...' limit 50`.
kevin: thanks. So triage steps: 1) enable sampling for tls_min_version (1% ingress), 2) add alert: >50 connections from unique src IPs with tls_min <1.2 in 5m to P1 channel, 3) run a quick RBAC audit for service accounts that can call KMS Decrypt (list), 4) verify OCSP/CRL latencies for certificate validation in EU region.
maya: I’ll open a PR for the envoy sampling. also updating nginx/edge TLS config to `ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on;` and disabling weak ciphers.
ashley: for RBAC — we should use `gcloud iam roles` check and export principals with `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` and `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypter`. I can run that and post results.
kevin: add temporary IAM deny binding for any stale service accounts that haven't rotated creds in 90d? We need process.
maya: note: any immediate mitigations we can apply without breaking legacy clients (some partner integrations still on old stacks)?
olga: fallback plan: use smart routing to send known legacy ASGs to a compatibility proxy cluster in a locked-down VPC (no access to customer KMS) and return 426 Upgrade Required for all others. Need SRE sign-off.
ashley: also consider enabling `TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV` validation at proxy level to prevent downgrade fallback. Envoy has `enable_tls_fallback_check` flag.
kevin: good. Once telemetry lands, add a dashboard: by region, by service, min_tls_version trend, and a per-ip outlier table.
maya: pushed the sampling PR (link: https://git.redwood/infra/envoy/+/2487). patch notes: sample 1% for 24h, then increase if we see noise.
ashley: on the vulnerability side — run `sslscan` against our endpoints and ensure we get TLS1.2/1.3 only. Put results into a simple CSV and attach to the ticket.
olga: and update our incident playbook: under "transport encryption anomaly": step 1 collect telemetry + KMS audit; step 2 confirm no Decrypt calls from unknown principals; step 3 rotate affected certs via ACME with short TTL (7d) if compromise suspected; step 4 escalate to legal if certs tied to customer-managed keys.
kevin: can someone update compliance: we need a note for SOC2 evidence that we performed detection and RBAC audit. add to the ticket with timestamps.
maya: will add evidence: logs, screenshot of dashboard, list of principals.
audit-bot: flagging: new metric `tls_min_version.sampled` emitted by infra at 2024-11-08T14:02:13Z.
kevin: thanks. final Q: does anyone have a list of proxies that need config rollout order to avoid global blips? we should do EU -> US -> APAC with canary percent.
maya: I’ll coordinate with eng-infra; propose rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2 hours per region.
ashley: sounds good. closing loop: create follow-up ticket for RBAC cleanup and KMS audit with owners @ashley @kevin @olga. :thumbsup:
